summary.headline: Heritage Foods Q1 FY27 revenue rose 18% to INR13,381 million, but EBITDA margin fell to 4.6% as raw milk costs rose 7% YoY.
summary.overview: Heritage posted its highest-ever quarterly revenue of INR13,381 million (+18% YoY), with EBITDA of INR619 million (4.6% margin) and PAT of INR150 million (1.9% margin). Value-added products (VAP) grew 40% YoY to INR5,636 million and reached 44% of consolidated revenue, while milk procurement cost rose 7% YoY to INR46.61/litre amid tight supply. Management attributed the margin squeeze to cow-milk price inflation, buffalo milk degrowth, higher SMP consumption and packaging costs, and said pricing actions are continuing into July. Liquid milk volume growth remains the main open problem.

segments.name: Milk
segments.commentary: Milk EBITDA margin 3.03% vs 5.8% in Q1 FY26; procurement volume 18.10 lakh litres/day (+2% YoY) while milk sales volume was stable. Buffalo milk volumes fell over 20% YoY.

segments.name: Value-added products
segments.commentary: VAP revenue INR5,636 million (+40%), EBITDA margin 8.06% vs 9.7% last year. Volume contributed ~35pp of growth and price ~5.12%. Paneer +33%, curd +26%, butter milk +60%, lassi +98%.

segments.name: Ice cream (Alpenvie, Get-A-Way)
segments.commentary: Ice cream crossed INR550 million (+65%); Alpenvie +44%; new facility at ~40% utilisation, producing both brands on a common platform. Ice cream is the highest-margin VAP per management.

segments.name: Heritage Nutrivet (animal nutrition)
segments.commentary: Revenue INR728 million (+37% YoY) with PBT of INR20 million despite elevated input costs.

segments.name: Ghee (consumer packs)
segments.commentary: EBITDA about -8.5%, improved from about -12% a year earlier; still loss-making.

guidance_outlook: Long-term target of 16-17% revenue growth, requiring milk growth of about 7-8% and VAP growth of about 25%.
VAP share of revenue targeted at around 50% by FY30, adding roughly 2-2.5pp per year.
Management aims for high single-digit EBITDA margin, not 6%; cites a 7-7.5% median over recent years.
FY27 capex expected at about INR250 crore: paneer and ghee projects under construction plus minor raw-milk procurement capex.
Management expects Q2 to look somewhat stronger than Q1 in animal nutrition, but gave no quantified EBITDA outlook for Heritage in Q2.
Further price increases are being taken in July across several markets for milk and VAP; no prices are expected to ease before the October-November buffalo flush.
capex_capacity: FY27 capex about INR250 crore: paneer project and ghee project under execution, plus minor raw milk procurement investment.
Ice cream facility commissioned and ramped to ~40% utilisation in Q1; common platform for Alpenvie and Get-A-Way.
Added close to 5,000 farmers in Q1 and plans another 5,000 in Q2; added about 1 lakh litres of distribution capacity in the quarter.
Heritage Novandie Foods became a wholly owned subsidiary (Livo high-protein yogurt); stake in Peanut Butter and Jelly Limited raised to 71%.
demand_pricing: Milk price realisation +4% YoY to INR58.68/litre; VAP price increase about 5.12% weighted average, so ~35pp of VAP growth is volume-driven.
Growth attributed about 80% to distribution expansion in existing geographies and about 20% to share gains; management claims share gains in curd, paneer and butter milk in organised channels.
Price actions were staggered: late Q4 FY26 hike, further hikes mid-May and early June, and more in July.
Curd fell to about 69% of VAP revenue (from about 75% earlier); paneer contributed about INR52 crore in the quarter.

Milk procurement: cow milk INR43.2/litre (Q4 FY26: INR42.10); buffalo milk INR65.99 (Q4: INR61.38). Management says gross margin fell about 2.5pp YoY from mix shift to cow milk, SMP consumption (~0.5%) and packaging costs (~30bps).
Liquid milk volume growth remains weak; management calls it the highest-priority problem, with MoM growth reported from March to July.

qa_highlights.question: Is milk procurement price easing during the summer flush, and what is the outlook for the October flush?
qa_highlights.answer: Samba Murthy said the expected April-May mini flush did not materialise, prices rose through March-June and are now stable; the company expects a stable to slightly higher Q2 and an October flush. Procurement volumes are being raised via village-level centres and farmer productivity.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the 40% VAP growth is price versus volume?
qa_highlights.answer: Srideep Kesavan said price contributed about 5.12% and the balance (~35%) is volume-driven, led by curd +26%, paneer +33% and butter milk +60%.

qa_highlights.question: Why did gross margin decline YoY despite a richer VAP mix?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited mix shift to cow milk (buffalo volumes down >20%), SMP consumed at higher volume and price (~0.5pp impact), and packaging costs (~30bps). Cow milk rose about INR1/litre QoQ.

qa_highlights.question: What is the break-even status of ghee and new geographies?
qa_highlights.answer: Ghee EBITDA improved to about -8.5% from about -12% a year ago; loss-making regions have narrowed losses, though still negative.

qa_highlights.question: Will VAP growth of 20-25% and milk EBITDA recovery lift margins to 6-7%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the target is high single-digit EBITDA, with raw milk price normalisation the main driver; about three-quarters of revenue is raw material, so VAP cannot yet offset milk volatility.

qa_highlights.question: What is the capex plan for FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: About INR250 crore, covering the paneer and ghee projects plus minor raw milk procurement capex.

risks_watch: Raw milk inflation: cow milk up about INR1/litre QoQ; El Nino and a weak southern monsoon may hit the October flush and fodder availability.
Liquid milk volume growth remains flat to weak and is the main drag on overhead absorption.
Feed and packaging input inflation: animal nutrition costs have risen month-on-month since Q3 FY26, and packaging costs rose due to the war.
Milk EBITDA at 3.03% and VAP at 8.06%; overall EBITDA margin 4.6% is well below the 7-8% normalised level discussed by analysts.
Management could not give Q2 margin guidance or a best/worst case for post-October procurement prices.
summary.management_tone: Confident on VAP growth, brand and distribution momentum, but cautious and non-committal on margins and procurement outlook. Management repeatedly declined to quantify Q2 or post-October prices, citing weather-driven unpredictability.
key_quotes: Consolidated revenue increased 18% year -on-year to INR13,381 million, marking another important milestone for Heritage.
So we are cycling a low base as well, number one.
So at this point in time, I should say that we are in the trough of it.
So I should admit that this is the main problem that we need to solve.
